chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Yaḥyā, from Mālik ibn Ashyam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Bashshār, who said:
Ibn Qiyāmā wrote a letter to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, saying in it: “How can you be an Imam while you do not have a child?”
So Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام answered him, as if angered: “And what has informed you that there will not be a child for me?”
By Allah, the days and nights will not pass until Allah grants me a male child through whom He will distinguish between the truth and falsehood.

key_terms.إِمَامًا: Imam; the divinely appointed leader whose authority is being questioned here
key_terms.الْبَاطِلِ: Falsehood; that which will be separated from truth through this sign
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: The truth; the side to be made distinct by means of the promised child
key_terms.الْمُغْضَبِ: Angered; describing the Imam’s stern response to the objection
key_terms.ذَكَرًا: A male child; the foretold son mentioned by the Imam
key_terms.وَلَدٌ: Child; specifically the issue of offspring raised in objection to the Imam’s status
key_terms.يَرْزُقَنِيَ: He will provide me; indicating Allah’s granting of a child as divine provision

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام respond when questioned about having no son?
ai.summary: This hadith records a challenge directed at Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding his Imamate in the absence of a son. The Imam replies firmly that Allah will grant him a male child, presenting this future birth as a sign through which truth would be distinguished from falsehood. In Shia tradition, this points to the birth of Imam al-Jawād عليه السلام and serves as evidence in discussions of Imamate.
